messages:
sara: FYI escalation from ACME via support: dedicated pool us-west-2 (svc-prod) sees ~60% throughput drop since 09:12 UTC. Customer reports many 429s and tail latency spikes. They say it's steady for ~20m. attaching logs they sent.

support-bot: New ticket #INC-9421 created and linked to this thread.

customer-ops: customer provided sample request ids: r_9a1, r_9a2, r_9a3. They included a short timeline and their observed p95 token/sec drop.

sara: quick snippets from customer (they pasted):
```
09:10:45 GET /v1/generate -> 200, 120ms
09:12:05 GET /v1/generate -> 429, retry
09:15:10 GET /v1/generate -> 503, downstream timeout
09:18:30 GET /v1/generate -> 200, 950ms
```
They said after 09:12 everything degraded.

jon: pinging eng-sre and runtime. Any autoscale events around 09:10-09:20?

infra-bot: Autoscale event: pool=dedicated-usw2-svc-prod scale_up triggered at 09:11:57 (delta +2 nodes). No further scale at 09:12-09:30.

maria: I see an odd pattern in sequencer logs — the continuous sequencer window started emitting small micro-batches (~2-3 requests) despite queue depth being moderate. That lowers GPU packing. attaching internal log snippet: 
```
09:11:58 sequencer: queue_depth=48, window_target=128, chosen_batch_tokens=40 -> microbatch_count=18
09:12:01 worker-3: started batch with 3 requests (total_tokens=56)
09:12:10 worker-7: prefill-rate drop detected, kv-cache miss spike
09:12:40 scheduler: quantum_slack=+30ms, elect_small_batch=true
```
Looks like sequencer favored low-latency decisions and broke packing.

kevin: did anything change in packing heuristics or routing policy in the last deploy?

maria: No deploys to runtime in that window. But there was a config push for per-route token ceiling (max_batch_tokens) at 09:09 — likely intended for a single tenant. If max_batch_tokens was set too low globally for this pool it would force many smaller batches.

elaine: I can confirm one recent config change: route /svc-prod set max_batch_tokens=64 (was 512) via config manager at 09:08 by ops. That would explain small batch token ceilings.

jon: that matches. If max_batch_tokens is 64 and typical request prefill is 80-120 tokens, sequencer will split and create many tiny batches -> inefficiency and autoscaler sees more latency, but node count didn't grow because scaling metric is based on cpu/util + inflight_requests. The microbatches keep inflight low but hurt throughput.

sara: customer also attached client patterns: mostly 1-2 short prompts but many small requests. Could be hitting new per-route limit unintentionally.

kevin: immediate mitigation options: 1) rollback the 09:08 config change, 2) increase local sequencer fill-window (batch_fill_timeout_ms) to allow more time to pack, 3) temporarily bump autoscale sensitivity to queue_depth. Which should we do first?

maria: I propose rollback config (fastest). Also set batch_fill_timeout_ms = 8ms -> 20ms to allow more grouping.

jon: rollback done (config-manager): /svc-prod max_batch_tokens reverted to 512 at 09:22 UTC.

infra-bot: Config change applied across pool at 09:22:41.

kevin: after rollback, we're still seeing elevated 429s but latency improving slowly. Could be stage-in period for cache and pipeline warmup. Monitor for 10m.

support-bot: Notified ACME that we've applied rollback and we're watching.

customer-ops: ACME reports error rate dropping after 09:28 and p95 improving at 09:33. They still saw a few 503s but overall better. :relieved: 

maria: Follow-ups: we should add a safety guard to prevent per-route max_batch_tokens from being set below a pool-min-threshold (e.g., 256) unless route-owned and marked experimental. Also add a sequencer metric: microbatch_ratio = microbatch_requests / total_batches to alert when >0.6.

jon: agree. Also recommend we add a short-term heuristic: if microbatch_ratio high and queue_depth > X, temporarily raise batch_fill_timeout_ms and disable elect_small_batch for that pool. Could be an automatic fallback.

kevin: action items: 1) infra: add pool-min threshold for max_batch_tokens (kevin) 2) eng-runtime: add microbatch_ratio metric and default auto-fallback (maria) 3) support: update runbook with this pattern and include how to check sequencer logs (sara).

elaine: logged infra task INFRA-702.

maria: I'll open runtime ticket RT-1184 for metric + fallback.

jon: nice work. marking this resolved for now but will keep on-call assigned for 24h to ensure no regressions. :thumbsup:

sara: ACME confirmed they're back to normal traffic pattern. closing escalation but will follow up on postmortem tomorrow with a short blameless note.

support-bot: Ticket #INC-9421 moved to resolved.

jon: TL;DR: root cause = accidental per-route max_batch_tokens change that forced sequencer into microbatching mode, reducing GPU packing and throughput. Rollback + slight fill-window increase restored effective throughput.
